items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-07-21
items.q: I can remember that very clearly. Now Mel Ott and several other white baseball players... they used to work out and practice together. That's what they did. So, uh... I had a fellow over there by the name of Mookow Miller...

ctx.x: Now the Algiers, okay, you have to back up. What was this?

It was Sandlot Baseball. Was it organized in any way? Well it was semi-organized. Because first I started playing with the Gretton All-Stars. It was a fellow by the name of Wesley Barrow who later became general manager of the Baltimore Eli Giants back in the 50s. And Wesley Barrow came out of Franklin, Louisiana. But he was a hefty man. But he had something like a YMCA, a USO, or whatever you want to call it. He always kept young people together. People like J.B. Spencer who also went to the Homestead Grays. And…
Now what were the professional black teams that played in this area? What did New Orleans have the professional black teams?

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-07-21
items.q: a lot of people didn't like OU alone but I liked him to a point because uh he I think he was trying to do something he wasn't totally white as such

ctx.x: what was I mean okay you couldn't go to the quarter I mean the club owners made it known that they didn't they didn't want blacks

that's right they made it known uh and then some of them did not but I tell you what broke up the French Quarter uh uh what made blacks started going to French Quarter uh Bill what is Bill's last name oh god dang it's on the tip of my tongue very good friend of mine and he loved Henry Desjua in fact uh the first time I really wanted to go into a club uh Alan Toussaint and myself was standing on ramp or uh standing down on Berber Street and up comes uh the piano player guy he's still playing he used to own a club…
